subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: Should OpenClaw add core/provider pace-aware quota policy for autonomous agents, and should the first product behavior be advisory-only visibility or active throttling/blocking?
rationale: The issue is not a narrow bug fix; it adds provider-specific quota semantics, config, persisted runtime state, and autonomous agent/subagent behavior that affect core/plugin boundaries and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Ship Advisory Pace Visibility First
options.body: Expose provider-owned pace/quota metadata in status and session_status without changing dispatch behavior, then evaluate opt-in enforcement once the contract is stable.

options.title: Add Opt-in Blocking Guardrail Now
options.body: Design a new config/state surface that can throttle or block autonomous runs when pace thresholds are crossed, with explicit upgrade tests and migration/doctor behavior.

options.title: Keep Pacing Outside Core For Now
options.body: Treat this as plugin/skill/operator policy until maintainers identify a missing core or plugin API that prevents external implementation.

recommendation.title: Ship Advisory Pace Visibility First
recommendation.body: Expose provider-owned pace/quota metadata in status and session_status without changing dispatch behavior, then evaluate opt-in enforcement once the contract is stable.

likelyOwner.reason: Most of the current provider usage/status foundation traces to this author, making them the strongest available code-history owner for the product/API decision.
